modelOfferedTools.name: read
modelOfferedTools.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

modelOfferedTools.name: write
modelOfferedTools.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

modelOfferedTools.name: edit
modelOfferedTools.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

modelOfferedTools.name: bash
modelOfferedTools.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns combined stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

first.reason: Isolation did not include scripts/set-password.mjs; missing module, not product failure

probeRetries: Initial version lookup used CJS require.resolve; pi-ai is ESM-only. Changed to import.meta.resolve.
First 1.4 run corrected assumptions: last registration wins, toolsAdded in transcript system messages, env factory also evaluated during chat; harness.snapshot is public API.
A2 large JSON stdout was truncated by process.exit before pipe flush. Awaited process.stdout.write callback, then reran all cases twice: 195/195 each.

cleanup.scope: Only per-case temporary directories removed; prepared isolated dependency install retained

conclusions.a1: Later same-name tool registration wins; CodingTools then custom bash safe is offered and executed. wrapTool and standalone read/write/edit/custom bash also pass.
conclusions.a2: 10 safe SIGKILL recoveries rerun execute with stable callId/taskId, clear old progress and retain only replay output from zero. 10 unsafe recoveries do not reenter and preserve old output with interrupted error. beforeTool runs only once before crash. Memo retains initial binding v1 even when restart proposes v2. Repeated c1 in same conversation yields different taskIds.
conclusions.a3: Same requestId across restart deduplicates to one submission/user/assistant/provider invocation. Different input payload silently reuses old input; different submission type throws.
conclusions.a4: Throwing env factory and exec-failing env both permit chat, settle bash as visible tool error, and continue model response. Factory evaluated even for chat. Exec-only failure does not block filesystem methods; read reaches local missing path.
conclusions.a5: Five concurrent WAL backups are integrity ok, same counts and keys in both tables, valid values, increasing counts; each backup 12288 bytes. Writer throttled to 4 rows/table per 20ms shared transaction.
conclusions.a6: Real BotRegistry.createBot cwd forwards unchanged to EnvTarget in both NodeExecutionEnv and fake-remote SandboxEnv. Missing cwd bash errors; local write creates parents, fake-remote write/read error.

designImplications: M1-04/06: runner identity must include durable control-store/deployment namespace + taskId; conversationId+callId collides across repeated model call IDs, and taskId alone collides across independent stores.

M1-05/06: safe replay skips beforeTool, so memoize initial binding in tool task and validate before remote effects inside execute; memo persists the first candidate, so compare current binding explicitly.
M1-06: only runner-backed idempotent execution may be safe; legacy shared env.exec fallback must not be blindly marked safe or it will rerun shell after crash.
M1-06: replay output from offset zero because durable prior progress is cleared.
M1-07/08: persist requestId with payload validation at application boundary if conflicting retries must be rejected; native input dedupe silently ignores changed content.
M1-05: either throwing env factory or a complete failing env can surface unready state; failing exec alone does not stop read/write. Do not use Node write behavior as workspace readiness enforcement.
